extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in computational media bias detection, NLP, and interdisciplinary media studies
extracted.subtask_short: systematic review of media bias detection
extracted.subtask_description: A systematic literature review and taxonomy of the forms and automated detection of media bias, synthesizing recent computational approaches (2019–2022) and identifying methodological strengths, weaknesses, and future directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Bias Taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: To structure our review and support a mutual understanding of bias across research domains, we introduce the Media Bias Taxonomy, which provides a coherent overview of the current state of research on media bias from different perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a coherent, cross-domain taxonomy to structure literature reviews and to enable consistent communication and comparison across studies of media bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformer-based classification approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Transformer-based classification approaches have led to significant improvements in recent years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider state-of-the-art transformer models when developing detection systems; evaluate their contributions relative to prior methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: These improvements include higher classification accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and compare classification accuracy (and related performance metrics) to quantify progress; ensure evaluation is rigorous and comparable across studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine-granular bias detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvements include the ability to detect more fine-granular types of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design models and annotation schemes to capture fine-grained bias categories rather than only coarse labels; evaluate models on their ability to distinguish nuanced bias types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.description: We have identified a lack of interdisciplinarity in existing projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster collaboration across disciplines (e.g., NLP, media studies, journalism, social sciences) to improve conceptualization, annotation, and evaluation of media bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of various types of media bias
rubrics_metrics.description: A need for more awareness of the various types of media bias to support methodologically thorough performance evaluations of media bias detection systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure datasets, annotations, and evaluations explicitly account for multiple bias forms; developers should be aware of the taxonomy of bias types when designing detection tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodologically thorough performance evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance evaluations of media bias detection systems should be methodologically thorough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt rigorous evaluation protocols that reflect the diversity of bias types and real-world conditions; avoid narrow or non-representative testing that overstates system capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of ML advancements with diverse bias assessment strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration of recent machine learning advancements with reliable and diverse bias assessment strategies from other research areas is the most promising area for future research contributions in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine cutting-edge ML models with assessment methods and evaluation perspectives from disciplines outside ML to create robust, trustworthy bias detection systems.
